rulings.why: The page tells these changes from the row (`can`), or the judge could not tell (`unclear`), but no check of the shape readings does: movedown:1.3: can: p553-strip800.jpg system 2: the four stanza rows sit note for note under one tune. On the note where stanza 1's database line 4 opens (the first quarter after two dotted halves), stanzas 3 and 4 print capitals after unpunctuated words, which only a line opening explains. On the system's first note, where the change would open the line, stanzas 2 to 4 print lowercase syllables. Stanza 1's row alone would not tell (the moved word is a title of God, the old opener the first-person pronoun), and the metre keeps lines 3 and 4 at 9 together, so this ruling rests on the alignment across stanzas. movedown:3.6: can: The header on p553-strip0.jpg prints 9.9.9.9. On p553-strip800.jpg systems 2 and 3, stanza 3's database lines 5+6 and 7+8 each sing 9 syllables, and the change moves a word across the boundary between those two 9-syllable lines, which leaves 8 and 10 and breaks the metre.
